newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet to debate Pekao group sale Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet to debate Pekao group sale Tuesday.

text.p: The Polish government will decide on April 22 on a timetable for the privatisation of a banking group led by the Pekao SA bank, a deputy treasury minister said.

"We expect that the privatisation would take place in the third or fourth quarter of this year. The decision will be taken by the council of ministers tomorrow," Piotr Czyzewski told reporters at a privatisation seminar.

The finance ministry has recently said that it wanted the Pekao group, which also involves Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA (PBG), Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy (BDK) and Pomorski Bank Kredytowy w Szczecinie SA (PBKS), to be sold next year.
Government officials have earlier said that the group's privatisation is likely to start with a flotation of its minority state on the Warsaw bourse.
Another stake could then be sold to institutional investors and a substantial equity is likely to be earmarked for a government programme to reform Poland's social security system.
Under the programme, the government is to issue bonds convertible into shares of companies undergoing privatisation.
